title: Assessment: Balancing Chemical Equations
description: Checkpoint assessment on balancing chemical equations using coefficients, atom counts, and the Law of Conservation of Mass.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why chemical equations must be balanced?
options: Balanced equations make all products more reactive.
Atoms are conserved, so each element must have the same atom count on both sides.
Subscripts must always be increased during reactions.
Products must always have smaller coefficients than reactants.
questions.explanation: Balanced equations show conservation of mass: atoms are rearranged but not created or destroyed.

questions.question: In 3CO2, how many oxygen atoms are represented?
questions.explanation: Each CO2 molecule has 2 oxygen atoms. The coefficient 3 means 3 x 2 = 6 oxygen atoms.

questions.question: Which coefficient set balances CH4 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O?
questions.explanation: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O has 1 C, 4 H, and 4 O atoms on both sides.

questions.question: Which equation correctly balances aluminum reacting with chlorine: Al + Cl2 -> AlCl3?
questions.explanation: 2Al + 3Cl2 -> 2AlCl3 gives 2 Al atoms and 6 Cl atoms on each side.

questions.question: True or False: The equation 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO is balanced.
questions.explanation: True. Both sides have 2 Mg atoms and 2 O atoms.

questions.question: True or False: The equation N2 + H2 -> 2NH3 is balanced.
questions.explanation: False. The nitrogen atoms are balanced, but hydrogen is not: left side has 2 H atoms and right side has 6 H atoms.

questions.question: Write the missing coefficient: N2 + __ H2 -> 2NH3
questions.explanation: The product side has 6 hydrogen atoms in 2NH3, so the reactant side needs 3H2.

questions.question: Balance the equation: H2 + O2 -> H2O
questions.explanation: First place 2 before H2O to balance oxygen, then place 2 before H2 to balance hydrogen.

questions.question: Balance the equation: Fe + O2 -> Fe2O3
questions.explanation: Use 2Fe2O3 to make 6 oxygen atoms on the product side, then use 3O2 and 4Fe on the reactant side.

questions.question: Balance the equation: C2H6 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O
questions.explanation: Balance carbon and hydrogen first, then oxygen. Multiplying by 2 avoids a fractional oxygen coefficient.

questions.question: A student balances H2 + O2 -> H2O by writing H2 + O2 -> H2O2. Explain the error and give the correct balanced equation.
questions.correctAnswer: The student changed the product formula, which changes water into hydrogen peroxide. The correct balanced equation is 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.
questions.explanation: Balancing must use coefficients, not changed subscripts. H2O and H2O2 are different substances.

questions.question: Describe a systematic strategy for balancing a simple chemical equation.
questions.correctAnswer: Write correct formulas, count atoms on both sides, adjust coefficients one element at a time, save hydrogen and oxygen for last when helpful, then recount every element and reduce to the smallest whole-number coefficients.
questions.explanation: A systematic strategy prevents random guessing and catches mistakes after each coefficient change.
